The improvement plan for the drones' Originium circuitry that Lorenz turned in a few weeks ago has been made real, and, to no one's surprise, it has posted rather brilliant results across a whole range of parameters.
This was never meant to be a research topic a thirteen-year-old would take part in. But in a place like Tecoma, children whose parents are researchers find it hard to come by anything more interesting than study, and no small number of the researchers themselves would like to hold a post that does not require dealing with disease and death every single day. The counseling team has done its best to propose all manner of measures for enriching recreational life, hoping to make living here a little easier and more comfortable, yet in a town 'dedicated to medical service' it is hard to avoid a certain repressive air, as though horsing around too much were a kind of wrongdoing.
And so, as long as a student is willing to learn, a teacher will dare to teach. This way of running a class, so utterly unlike the standard model of instruction, is nothing new in Tecoma, and Lorenz is hardly the only youthful face to be found in an institution of higher learning. What is more, she is the child of 'that Robert.'
'Professor, though, there's something I don't quite understand.' Lorenz watched the drone's flight path thoughtfully. 'You said I shouldn't achieve the optimization by using my Originium Arts to interfere with the Originium chip directly, in real time. So I spent over a year learning how to reach an approximate effect with Originium circuits.'
'That's right. Originium Arts that belong to you alone can hardly be mass-produced the way Originium circuits can, so they can never become a mature technology of broad application.'
'But I've found that you were wrong. That all of us had it wrong. This isn't a good enough research topic.' Lorenz broke into the heartfelt smile a child wears when regarding her own masterpiece, which the professor found somewhat unsettling. 'As a control, I also tried using Originium Arts to write portions of the operational logic separately into several pieces of Originium. After wiring them into the circuit and adding an inverter for debugging, I believe the result is very nearly equivalent to an imitation of Originium Arts.'
'Perhaps it is... but you shouldn't have done that. There is still a great deal about Originium Arts we have yet to map out. An operation like that is truly dangerous.'
'Yes, Originium Arts are like a black box. It seems we can call upon energy to do what we want done without knowing the principle behind it. Which is why, after this past year and more of study, I'm all the more certain: Originium can, to a certain degree, receive our will and realize it, regardless of whether we ourselves possess enough knowledge of the process by which it does so.'
'You are treating Originium as a wish-granting machine of unknown principle. That is not the rigorous view one ought to take toward science.'
'So my hypothesis is this: the medium Originium relies upon when it interferes with matter or energy is the same one it relies upon when it receives instructions, and it is neither wave nor particle. Its nature is something like a ghost, or say, "information." That would also explain why we observe no appreciable change in mass or energy when Originium is used. I don't imagine I'm the first to put forward such a hypothesis, but don't you think this is the one topic in this age truly worth anything?'
'...You already held this hypothesis long before you ever came to my class, didn't you?'
'Yes. It was the first time I played with an Originium camera, when I saw my late father through the viewfinder.'
'I'm sorry.'
'No, Professor. That is not the rigorous view one ought to take toward science.' Not a flicker crossed the girl's face. 'I'm glad my conjecture has received its first confirmation, and I'm willing to walk further down this road.'
